why: git calls a blob binary when its first 8000 bytes hold a NUL, and a small compressed or encrypted blob often holds none: 243 random bytes miss one about 39% of the time. Read as text, every stray C0 byte in it was a finding, and an honest repository of extracted firmware failed with 25,972 of them. The pass side is assets/radio.dat, 243 fixed high-entropy bytes behind a zlib header with no 0x00: the window is not UTF-8 and most of it decodes to replacement characters or C0, so it is binary. The fail side is the same bytes under a .txt name, which must be text whatever it holds, so its controls still fail. Drop the entropy test and the pass side goes red; apply it to must-be-text names and the fail side goes green.
